intro.lore: In 4E 210, nearly a decade after the Dragon Crisis, Skyrim stands transformed. To combat the Aldmeri Dominion, former enemies united alongside Hammerfell to sign The Treaty of The Nine Holds, successfully expelling the Thalmor in the brutal Second Great War. Today, the victorious but scarred province is split into three political zones: the Western Imperial Legion, the Eastern Stormcloaks, and the neutral central hub of Whiterun. As this new era begins, Skyrim's ultimate fate remains undecided.

choice.permadeathConfirm: Warning: this will kill your character and make them unplayable. Everything will be lootable and your body will remain.
choice.resurrectConfirm: This will release you at full health where you are standing. This is to be used in the event of a glitch — abuse will result in a ban. All uses are logged, and if you die again to the same player you will be force permanently killed.
choice.templeConfirm: This will send you to the nearest temple normally, except with full health, skipping the recovery system. This is an optional choice available to all players, with the catch that you cannot return to where you died for one hour.

death.title: You have died!
death.respawnBefore: You will automatically respawn at the nearest temple in
death.body1: If you do nothing, normal respawn rules apply. You were found near death and brought to a temple by a traveler. You only remember vague details about your death, not enough to identify your killer if there was one.
death.body2: You will have 1 HP and naturally heal 1 point every 8 hours (even while logged off). A healer can accelerate this to 5 HP every 8 hours.

confirm.voidKeysBody: Every key cut for this property stops working, including the ones you hold.
confirm.breakLockBody: The owner and every key holder lose it, every key stops working and anyone may claim it.
confirm.pinNoteBody: It leaves your pack. Whoever takes it down gets it.
confirm.giveFactionBody: It stops being yours and stays with the faction whoever leads it. Its ranks that open faction doors use it, its property managers run it, and every key cut so far stops working.

housing.claimable: Nobody has claimed this yet. Claiming uses up one lock.
housing.factionClaimHint: A faction claim belongs to the faction, not to you, and stays with it whoever leads it.
housing.hintSidesExit: A locked entrance stops everyone coming in, a locked exit everyone going out, you included, until it is unlocked here. Leave the exit open and nobody is shut inside. A key lets its holder lock and unlock both too: trade it or leave it in a chest. Void all keys cancels every copy.
housing.hintSides: A locked entrance stops everyone coming in, you included, until it is unlocked here. Nobody is ever shut inside: the way out always opens. A key lets its holder lock and unlock it too: trade it or leave it in a chest. Void all keys cancels every copy.
housing.hintDoor: A locked door stops everyone, you included, until it is unlocked here. A key lets its holder lock and unlock it too: trade it or leave it in a chest. Void all keys cancels every copy.
housing.factionManagerHint: Every rank of {faction} that opens faction doors locks and unlocks this too. Its property managers rename it, cut and void keys, transfer it or give it up.
housing.factionMemberHint: Your rank in {faction} lets you lock and unlock this from here.
housing.nameChars: Letters, numbers, spaces, apostrophes and dashes only.

masteryFreeWork.blacksmith: nails, iron fittings, locks and hinges at the forge, the Bandit armour tempers, and sea salt and charcoal at the smelter.
masteryFreeWork.tailor: leather strips, fur armour and blank parchment, journals and books at the tanning rack, thread and the roughspun tunic at the loom, and the Bandit armour tempers.
masteryFreeWork.woodworker: the blank parchment, journal and book at the woodcrafting bench, charcoal, and chopping wood at a chopping block.
masteryFreeWork.alchemist: honey at the alchemy lab, any drink at a meadery boiler, and picking plants and trees.
masteryFreeWork.cook: salmon steak, rabbit haunch, pheasant roast, chicken breast and honey at the cooking pot, and any drink at a meadery boiler.
masteryFreeWork.miner: mining iron veins and sea salt deposits, and sea salt and charcoal at the smelter.
masteryFreeWork.farmer: picking plants and trees, and crops with a hoe.
masteryFreeWork.hunter: killing animals, and the free recipes of the tanning rack.
masteryFreeWork.warrior: any kill of a person or creature.
masteryFreeWork.mage: casting any spell; learn one from a tome first.

blacksmith.r4: Glass, Ebony, and Master Racial Equipment

woodworker.r4: Glass, Ebony, and Master Racial Equipment

alchemist.r1: Minor potions of healing, magicka and stamina.
alchemist.r2: Weak poisons, and the weak aversions.
alchemist.r3: The plain potions of every school, attribute and resistance.
alchemist.r4: Draughts, philters and elixirs: the strongest work of the lab.

cook.r3: Baking: bread, sweet rolls and dumplings.
cook.r5: A Feast Fit for a Jarl

hunter.r1: The pelts and hides only a hunter can take whole.
hunter.r2: A faster draw and a steadier aim afield.
hunter.r3: A longer hold on a drawn bow.
hunter.r4: The full craft of the chase.

warrior.r1: Lighter power attacks with one hand or two, and deeper wind.
warrior.r2: A faster off hand, the power bash, a shield carried at speed, and light armour that weighs nothing.
warrior.r3: The charge, and heavy armour that weighs nothing.
warrior.r4: The sweeping blow, a warmaster's reach, and a heavier pack.

polymorph.hint: Transform turns you, or the player selected on the Players tab, into the race; double click does it at once. Revert puts the character's own race, face and gear back, and so do logging out, a crash and a server restart. Creature forms take the gear off until Revert. Races without a skeleton and races marked as a crash risk (flying, immobile and water-only races, the beast forms, horses, props and effects) are refused.
